To gain deeper insights into the ROP of M1, we performed
density functional theory (DFT) calculations, in which both
the DBU-initiated zwitterionic pathway and the anionic
pathway were considered. In general, La(OTf) preferentially
coordinates to
-dicarbonyls, giving energetically stable
species A (by 17.8 kcal/mol) and D (by 15.5 kcal/mol). In
the DBU-initiated zwitterionic pathway (Figure 4, left),
although both reactions are significantly exothermic, the
nucleophilic addition of DBU to A at the C -position, via
the transition state TS1, is 1.8 kcal/mol kinetically more
favorable than the addition at inner
position, via the
transition state TS2. In the anionic pathway (Figure 4, right),
we found that the deprotonation of D by DBU through TS3
( \Delta G ^ { \ddagger } = 8 . 1
kcal/mol) is much easier than DBU initiations
( \Delta G ^ { \ddagger } = 2 0 . 9
and 22.7 kcal/mol), thereby outcompeting the
zwitterionic pathway.
Starting from the anionic species
\mathbf { E } ,
both local
( \mathbf { C } _ { 2 }
-selective)
and vinylogous
( \mathrm { C } _ { 5 }
-selective) ring-opening reactions are
thermodynamically favorable. However, the latter process via
TS5 is kinetically more favorable, by 1.5 kcal/mol, than the
former via TS4. These findings align with our experimental
observations, which suggest a predominant vinylogous anionic
ROP mechanism. Due to the release of ring strain energy,
further propagation from the propargyl carbon anion G with A
is thermodynamically favorable, with an energy barrier of 19.2
kcal/mol. By contrast, the protonation reaction of the anion G
with DBU-H<sup>+</sup> has to overcome an energy barrier of 28.2 kcal/
mol. Notwithstanding, the tolerance to specific amounts of
protic additives in the polymerization (Table 1, entries 5 and
6) supports the viability of reversible termination. Arguably,
barrierless chain transfer events via proton exchange likely
dominate the reversible deactivation equilibrium (Table 1,
entries 7−11).
In summary, we have developed a La(OTf) /DBU/C−H
triple system for the first vinylogous anionic ROP of
vinylidenecyclopropane monomers, producing diverse main-
chain alkyne polymers with tailored molecular weights and low
dispersity. A number of
\mathsf { s p } ^ { 3 }
and
\mathsf { s p } ^ { 2 }
C−H bonds qualify in
initiating the polymerization and regulating the chain growth
via reversible termination and chain transfer. This strategy
enables unprecedented polymer chemistry of cyclopropanes
and is expected to transform precision polymer synthesis and
related materials science.
